newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Interconnector gas pipeline construction starts.
newsitem.headline: Interconnector gas pipeline construction starts.

text.p: Construction started Monday on the Interconnector gas pipeline, the first gas pipeline to link Britain with continental Europe.
"The works started today," said a spokeswoman for natural gas distributor Distrigas/Distrigaz, which has a five percent stake in the consortium. The pipeline is due to come on stream in October 1998.

The 23 billion Belgian franc project will link British and continental gas transmission systems, carrying up to 20 billion cubic metres of natural gas a year from Britain's Bacton, Norfolk, terminal to Zeebrugge. About 8.5 billion cubic metres a year will flow in the opposite direction.

Partners in the Interconnector consortium are British Gas Plc, British Petroleum Co Plc, Elf Aquitaine of France, Russia's Gazprom, Distrigas, German Ruhrgas, Amerada Hess Corp of the U.S. and National Power Plc of the UK.
A similar pipeline from the Norwegian sector of the North Sea to Dunkirk in France, only 60 km from Zeebrugge, will open in 1998.
